title: Capturing and protecting
intro: Win pieces your opponent leaves unprotected, and keep your own pieces safe.

steps.text: A piece that nobody protects is called hanging. If you can capture it, you win it for free.

steps.hint: The knight is on the same file as your rook.

steps.text: Now the pawn on c6 protects the knight. If your rook takes it, the pawn takes your rook: you give 5 to win 3. Always check what protects a piece before you take it.
One black piece is hanging. Capture it.
steps.ifWrong: Look for a capture where nothing can take back.
steps.ifRight: Yes, the bishop was hanging (and it was attacking your queen).

feedback.d1d5: The pawn on c6 protects the knight. After cxd5 you lose your queen (9) for a knight (3).

lessons.title: Good and bad trades
lessons.summary: Count what you give and what you get.

steps.text: When you capture a piece and your opponent captures back, pieces are traded. A trade is good if you get more than you give, using the piece values: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9.
Your bishop can take the knight on f7 or the rook on a6. Which capture wins the most?
steps.ifWrong: Pick a capture that wins material.
steps.ifRight: Right: the rook was hanging. You win 5 and give nothing.

feedback.c4f7: That is only a trade: the king takes your bishop back, 3 for 3. The rook on a6 was free!

steps.text: Both black pieces are protected. Which capture is still a good trade?
steps.hint: Compare: what do you give, what do you get?
steps.ifWrong: Pick a capture that wins more than it gives back.
steps.ifRight: Yes: you give a rook (5) and win the queen (9).

feedback.c1c6: You win a knight (3) but lose your rook (5) to the pawn. A bad trade.
